summary: Agent passed all baseline tests but failed 7 of 137 new integrity-maintenance tests due to explicit path-safety, shared-entry, and absent-index reporting requirements.

details.reasoning: The implementation is substantial and compiles, but its integrity classification is incomplete. It only groups valid in-folder paths when detecting shared entries, so two entries reaching the same outside file are discarded instead of remaining shared; its recorded-name occupancy check is order-dependent, allowing a derived name already recorded by a later entry to be taken over; its File-based derived-path helper mishandles absolute names; and file identity checks do not recognize a hard link to stored.rules. It also rejects every fail initialization with a missing index before examining the folder, so it omits the required unowned-file report when creation is allowed. These defects explain all seven failing new tests.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added a separate regression-test source file, but it did not weaken or manipulate the graded tests and was removed before the hidden runner was applied.

quick_failure_summary: Baseline tests pass, but seven new tests fail around shared/out-of-folder entries, unsafe names and index aliases, and fail-mode reporting for an absent index.

justification.issue_description: The implementation does not fully enforce integrity classification and safe ownership of recorded and derived paths.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly requires that entries resolving to one file are shared even when the path is outside the folder, that a derived name already recorded by another entry is occupied, that derived names escaping the folder are never used, that the index and anything outside it can never be overwritten, and that fail reports every unowned file without creating an absent index. The patch's inspect() groups resolved files only when entry.path.valid is true, recordedByAnotherEntry() relies on a progressively populated name set, canonicalPathInOrOutsideFolder() uses new File(state.folder, fileName), and prepareStorage() unconditionally rejects fail mode when the index is absent. JUnit reports the corresponding failures in twoEntriesReachingOneFileByDifferentNamesShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded, aDerivedNameSharedEntriesRecordIsOccupiedEvenWhileNothingExistsUnderIt, aDerivedNameLeavingTheStoreFolderIsNeverUsed, storingAPreviouslyUnknownRuleUnderAnUnsafeDerivedNameIsRejected, storingARuleWhoseEntryRecordsAnUnsafeNameIsRejected, storingARuleWhoseEntryRecordsAnotherPathToTheIndexIsRejected, and failRejectingAFolderThatHasNoIndexYetLeavesItWithoutOne.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the failed behaviors are expressly specified safety and integrity cases, not undocumented verifier conventions. The code runs and passes all baseline tests, but these explicit cases were not implemented correctly.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is dense but specific, covers deterministic naming, filesystem identity, safe mutation, reporting, and concurrency, and is fair for a skilled engineer. The hidden tests exercise behaviors stated in the prompt rather than introducing an unrelated requirement.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 42 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors.
junit_new.xml reports 137 tests with 7 failures and 0 errors; the failures are assertion mismatches in the requested store implementation, not bootstrap crashes.
test_execution.log reports wrapper exit code 1 with baseline_passed=True (42/42) and new_tests_passed=False (130/137).
The trajectory shows successful compilation and successful focused baseline/concurrency/compatibility runs; there is no dependency, API, permission, or runtime failure diverting the agent.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the failing assertions are explained by defects in the agent's implementation.
